title: Shadow explorers
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: trace a shadow and see what changes.

body.heading: Set up together
paragraphs: Ask an adult to choose a safe, flat outdoor spot away from roads. Place a small, sturdy toy on a sheet of paper in sunlight. Keep the paper from blowing away without using anything sharp.
The adult stays with you. Never look directly at the Sun, even for a moment. If it is too hot, wet, or uncomfortable, save the activity for another time.

body.heading: Trace, wait, compare
paragraphs: Draw around the toy’s shadow. The adult can write the time next to your line. Leave the toy and paper in the same place and return together later.
Use a different colour to trace the new shadow. Has its direction or length changed? Clouds might make it faint. “We could not see a clear shadow” is a useful observation too.

body.heading: Take the wonder off-screen
paragraphs: Talk about which line is longer. You can compare with a strip of paper instead of a ruler. Your drawing records what you saw; it does not have to look like anyone else’s.
For a screen-free extension, hold your hand near a wall while an adult shines an ordinary torch. Move the light, and describe how the shadow changes. Never shine the torch into anyone’s eyes.

takeaway: A shadow shows where light is blocked. Try changing the light and noticing what happens.
safetyNotes: Never look directly at the Sun. Choose a safe location and suitable weather.
screenFreeExtension: Try the final pretend scene or light experiment together away from the website.
